definition: The vomeronasal system is a chemosensory pathway involved in detecting socially relevant odor signals. In female mice, the packet describes it as mediating pre-implantation pregnancy block triggered by unfamiliar male chemosignals and as part of the pathway through which mate-related signals can be selectively suppressed.

reasons: The definition claims the vomeronasal system is a general chemosensory pathway for detecting “socially relevant odor signals,” but the packet only mentions chemosensory signals from unfamiliar males in the context of pregnancy block; it does not describe “socially relevant odor signals” as the system’s role.

The remaining claims about female mice are supported in the packet (pre-implantation pregnancy block mediated by the vomeronasal system; selective inhibition of the mate’s pregnancy-blocking chemosignals at the level of the accessory olfactory bulb).

The packet supports the vomeronasal system as part of a female-mouse pregnancy-block pathway, but not the broad gloss that it is a general chemosensory pathway for detecting socially relevant odor signals.

The packet supports pre-implantation pregnancy block and selective gating of male chemosensory information, but it does not support the more general phrasing about "mate-related signals" being selectively suppressed as a defining function of the system.
The field is not well supported here: the source is about olfactory/neural signaling in mice, not a cognition concept in the usual psychology/counselling sense.
